entries.text: The one who stole it drinks here most nights. Pays in coin nobody recognises
A fence by the docks swears it passed through last month. Nobody's seen that fence since
It was stolen to order, mark my words. Someone wanted a thing that {f:function}, and paid ahead
Heard {npcname}'s heirs put up a reward. Heard the thief put up a bigger one to keep folk quiet
My cousin bought it off a cart for three silver. Two very large strangers bought it back, very politely
Don't touch it. My uncle held it once, and now my uncle won't go near a mirror
Everyone who ever owned {name} died before their fortieth winter. Everyone we know about, anyway
Oh, it {f:function}, right enough. But it takes something back every time
The priest says carry it home to {the:origin} and the curse lifts. The priest also drinks
My gran swore it hums the night before a death. Hummed at my wedding, too
Whoever holds it owes someone. Nobody says who, and nobody says it loudly
They say {npcname} gave up something they can't buy back to get it. A shadow, or a name
There's a contract, see. Signed in something that isn't ink, and it's coming due soon
Someone offered it to my friend for free. Nothing that {f:function} comes free, I said
The collector came asking after it last winter. Polite as anything. Left no footprints in the snow
It wasn't lost, whatever the heirs say. Somebody close sold {npcname} out, and everyone at that table knows who
Ask the old steward how they got so rich so fast. Go on, ask. Watch their hands
Best friends, the two of them. Then one had {name} and the other had a knife in the back
The one who got betrayed is still alive, they say. Alive, and very, very patient
Whoever did it still comes in here. Buys rounds. Laughs too loud. You'd never guess
A treasure-hunter I know swears they saw it glinting in the dark. Then they stopped talking about it
Half the fortune-seekers in town are hunting it. The other half are selling them fake maps
My granddad had a map to {name}. Used it to patch the roof
Lost? Not lost. Someone knows exactly where it is and wants the rest of us looking elsewhere
Every spring some fool goes looking for it. Every summer we hold a small funeral
I swear it moved. Left it on the table, came back, and it was facing the door
They say it {f:function} on its own now, whenever the mood takes it
It talks, apparently. Mostly at night. Mostly about {npcname}
My mate kept it in a drawer. Woke up with it on the pillow, watching
It's not a thing any more, if you ask me. It's a someone, and it's in a mood
Leave it be. It's guarding something, and you don't want to meet what it's guarding
Folk leave flowers by it. Nobody remembers why, but nobody dares stop
The old ones say the night it's moved, whatever it's been keeping in gets out
Sure, it {f:function}, but that's not its job. Its job is keeping something shut
A lord tried to sell it once. The crops failed that same week, every field
There's a prophecy about {name}. Every seer in town gives a different ending, and they all charge
Some farm kid's been dreaming of it every night. Kid's never even heard of it
The cult on the hill wants it badly. The temple wants it worse, and the temple has more swords
My aunt read it in the tea leaves: that thing, a stranger at the door, and a very bad winter
Old verse says it'll be found when the river runs backwards. The river's been acting strange
Came from {the:origin}, they say, and the folk there want it back more than anyone
Whatever you heard about it, halve it. Then double the danger
